blocks.text: Adapter parsers own provider-local `RawEvent` envelopes. Adapter translation maps those envelopes into provider-neutral run-scope events; supervisor draft construction maps those run events into canonical IR event types.

items: Known provider raw types map to registered domain `EventType` values through adapter translation and `providerEventDraft`.
Unknown provider raw types must become non-transition provider observations or logs; they must not create FSM authority.
Known raw types with unknown fields preserve unknown source data only through explicitly modeled draft payload/unknown surfaces.
Derived meaning must be marked by the translating adapter when provider output did not directly report the fact.
Provider transition-after-side facts are drafts only; ingest/orchestration decides state transitions.

blocks.text: The adjacent [`event-ingestor-contract.md`](event-ingestor-contract.md) owns final `CanonicalEvent` envelope completion and validation.

RIID-5827: Claude partial text is forwarded without duplicating final blocks. Codex native turn status distinguishes completed, failed and interrupted even after partial output; idle/ready thread availability does not complete a turn. Native approval responses retain JSON-RPC request identity. The SaaS adapter forwards every supervisor-batched partial snapshot without a second debounce.

RIID-5816: Claude native can_use_tool and legacy permission_request preserve original input in a run-local driver, while redacted ToolRef arguments remain diagnostic only. Its stdin stays open until shutdown. Error, budget and turn-limit results retain failure reasons instead of reporting success.

RIID-6005: Codex run events belong to the thread and turn selected by the daemon handshake. Events from child threads or other turns cannot contribute output, change session identity, request approval, or terminate the parent run. Only the parent turn result completes the run; thread activity and individual item completion are not successful run results. Completed parent agentMessage items supply the final result body (final_answer, or an absent phase for older runtimes); commentary remains progress only. A completed modern turn with streamed text but no final message fails instead of promoting progress into a result. Explicit native failure/interruption and legacy unscoped result output remain supported.
